nahhas-irab:103-103.t:
Al-Ḥasan read إِنَّما يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ, with «بشر» without tanwīn (nunation) and «اللسان» with the definite article, اللسان being nominative. «بشر» is nominative (marfūʿ) by its verb, and «اللسان» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أعجميّ». The tanwīn was dropped from «بشر» because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and Sībawayh cited:
[al-Mutaqārib] 264-
ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا
(Gloss: "…nor remembering Allah except a little" — with ذاكر left without tanwīn before الله.)
Similar to it is the reading of whoever read قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2], and likewise وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ [Yā Sīn: 20] with النهار in the accusative. «[Translator's note: the verse is Yā Sīn 36:40, not 20, as printed in the source.]» The people of Medina «[Translator's note: the source has «أقل المدينة», evidently a misprint for «أهل المدينة».]» and the people of Basra read يُلْحِدُونَ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the Kufans read يلحدون with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ. The more eloquent usage is «يلحدون»; from it one says: رجل ملحد, i.e. a man inclining away from the truth. This is made clear by وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ [al-Ḥajj: 25], for this is from ألحد يلحد and nothing else. One says: لحدت القبر, i.e. I made a niche (laḥd) in it, and ألحدت الميّت, i.e. I put the dead man in the niche.
وَهذا لِسانٌ: it is said that it means the Qur'an; it called it a "tongue" by extension of usage, just as one says "So-and-so speaks with the tongue of the Arabs", i.e. in their language. Likewise اللسان الذي يلحدون إليه means his speech; on this basis a message is called a "tongue", as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 265-
لسان السّوء تهديها إلينا
(Gloss: "an evil tongue [i.e. an evil message] that you send to us".)

nahhas-irab:106-106.t:
مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِهِ: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for «الكاذبين».
إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā) in an exception. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: except one who is coerced.
Such a person may say what outwardly is a lie and disbelief while not believing it; but he may not tell an outright lie in any way. Rather he says "So-and-so is a liar" meaning "according to their claim", or he means by it someone other than the Prophet ﷺ who really is a liar; for lying is foul, and it is not possible that Allah should permit it in any circumstance. The proof of its foulness is that the one who utters it is not trusted in what he reports.
وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and it is an explanation of what came before. مَنْ شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ is a mubtadaʾ. فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ is in the position of the khabar.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: اسْتَحَبُّوا الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ: al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: لا جَرَمَ is only ever a reply. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: مِنْ بَعْدِها, i.e. after the trial (fitna).

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: يَوْمَ تَأْتِي is in the position of the accusative, i.e. Forgiving, Merciful on the day every soul comes; and it may have the meaning: and remember the day every soul comes.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً, i.e. the likeness of a town. فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ اللَّهِ: أنعم is the plural of نعمة according to Sībawayh; Quṭrub said: it is the plural of نعم, like ودّ and أدود.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ: الكذب is accusative, with the meaning "because of your tongues' describing the lie". And he said: الكذب — he throws the vowel of the dāl onto the kāf. «[Translator's note: the text here is as printed; it apparently refers to a reading الكِذْب, with the vowel of the dhāl transferred to the kāf.]» The people of Syria, or some of them, read وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ as a naʿt (adjective) of the tongues «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading الكُذُبُ in the nominative, qualifying ألسنتكم; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]», and al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa and Abū Maʿmar read لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ in the genitive, as a naʿt of ما or a badal (substitute) for it. «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading الكَذِبِ in the genitive; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]»

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ: on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. their enjoyment in this world is a little enjoyment, i.e. the length of their remaining. Outside the Qur'an متاعا would be permissible as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they are given enjoyment (يمتعون متاعا).

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: كانَ أُمَّةً: the khabar (predicate) of kāna. قانِتاً: a naʿt (adjective) or a second khabar. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned وَلَمْ يَكُ in more than one place.

nahhas-irab:124-124.t: إِنَّما جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ: some of them said: we do not want Friday, and some of them said: we do not want the Sabbath; so rest on the day of the Sabbath was made obligatory upon them.

nahhas-irab:127-127.t:
وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ: it is said that the meaning is: do not grieve over the unbelievers, for your duty is only to call them to faith; and it is said that the meaning is: do not grieve over the martyrs, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has rewarded them — among them was Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, may Allah be pleased with him, and concerning him was revealed وَإِنْ عاقَبْتُمْ فَعاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ [al-Naḥl: 126]. وَلا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ refers to the unbelievers; no one said otherwise. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām reported that Nāfiʿ read وَلا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ with kasra on the ḍād. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is not known from Nāfiʿ. The Kufans — al-Farrāʾ and others — said: «الضيق» with fatḥa on the ḍād is in the heart and the breast, and «الضيق» with kasra on the ḍād is in a garment, a house and the like of what is seen. Al-Farrāʾ said: if you see الضيق with fatḥa on the ḍād occurring in the place of الضّيق, it is a lightened form of ضيّق or the plural of ضيقة. The Basrans know nothing of this distinction; they said: if you mean the maṣdar (verbal noun) you say الضيق, as you say البيع, and if you mean the noun you say الضيق, as you say العلم; and they permitted lightening ضيّق.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: الَّذِينَ is genitive through مع being annexed to it, because مع according to al-Khalīl is a noun when you give the ʿayn a fatḥa, and if you make it quiescent it is a particle. وَالَّذِينَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf). هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), within the ṣila (relative clause).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: أَتى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: among the best of what has been said about its meaning is the saying of al-Ḍaḥḥāk that it is the Qur'an; and it was said: it is the victory of the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever said it is the Resurrection made it figurative in one of two ways: «أتى» means "has drawn near", or «أتى» means "will come" — except that Sībawayh does not allow faʿala (the past) to mean yafʿalu (the imperfect), though he allows yafʿalu to mean faʿala, because it may be [a narrated state] reported. فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ: a prohibition carrying the sense of threat.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: وَإِذا بَدَّلْنا آيَةً مَكانَ آيَةٍ: and that is the abrogating and the abrogated, for the good that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows to be in that; they became confused by it and said إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and likewise بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَما ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوانُهُ: al-Akhfash said: i.e. He created and spread.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: وَأَنْهاراً وَسُبُلًا: he said: i.e. "and He made". Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of وَأَلْقى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ is "and He made", so for this reason "and He made" was implied in the second. أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ is in the position of an accusative; the implied structure according to the Basrans is "out of aversion that it should sway with you", and according to the Kufans "lest it sway with you".

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: أَنْ أَنْذِرُوا: Abū Isḥāq said: «أن» is in the position of a genitive as a badal (substitute) from (الروح), the implied structure being: "He sends down the angels with: warn the people of disbelief and sins", i.e. caution them that لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاتَّقُونِ. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, pointed to His oneness, saying, exalted be His praise: خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (لا يخلقون شيئا). Al-Akhfash said: وَالنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّراتٌ [verse: 12], i.e. "and He created and subjected". Al-Farrāʾ related: مخرت السفينة تمخر وتمخر, when the ship makes a sound in its course. «[Translator's note: the two imperfect forms (with fatḥa and with ḍamma) are not distinguished by vowelling in the source; the remark concerns مَواخِرَ in verse 14.]» Abū Isḥāq said: (النجم) and (النجوم) are the same.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْياءٍ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead". Al-Kisāʾī said: and the accusative is permissible by "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ) and the verb. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket after «القطع».]» أَيَّانَ is in the position of an accusative. يُبْعَثُونَ. But it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, because it carries the sense of interrogation, so it had to be uninflected; its nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. When two quiescent letters meet in one word, the second is given fatḥa, and if they are in two words, the first is given kasra. This is the view of the Kufans. As for the Basrans, the rule for two quiescent letters when they meet is, according to them, that one of them be given kasra unless some special cause occurs; and what necessitated this is that kasra is the sister of the jussive. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: [it is] because what is inflected and fully declined is never given kasra except with tanwīn. When the first quiescent letter is an alif, then fatḥa is preferable according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because fatḥa is of the same kind as alif. They said: if you named a man (إسحار) and then truncated it [in the vocative, tarkhīm], you would say يا إسحار أقبل ("O Isḥār, come"), giving the rāʾ fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since an alif precedes it. «[Translator's note: the truncated form intended is إسحارّ → يا إسحارَّ; the doubling is not marked in the source.]» Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ with kasra on the hamza [i.e. إِيَّانَ]. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the dialect of Sulaym.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: We have mentioned لا جَرَمَ أَنَّ in another place than this.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ: (ما) is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) means "which" (الذي) and is the khabar (predicate) of «ما». قالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ: with an implied mubtadaʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. "it is the tales of the ancients". Al-Akhfash said: the answer is referred back to the first utterance, so since «ما» was in the position of a nominative, [the answer] was put in the nominative. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "that which He sent down", i.e. "that which you claim He sent down is the tales of the ancients", i.e. lies. Others said: this is by way of mockery, i.e. some of them say to others: "What has your Lord sent down?", and the one answering says: "Tales of the ancients", not acknowledging that He sent down anything; for this reason it is nominative. The grammarians allowed: ماذا تعلّمت أنحوا أم شعرا ("What did you learn — grammar or poetry?") with the accusative and the nominative: the nominative according to what has preceded, and the accusative on the basis that «ذا» is redundant (zāʾida), meaning "what thing did you learn?". But if you say من ذا كلّمت أزيدا أم عمرا ("Who is it you spoke to — Zayd or ʿAmr?"), «من ذا» would not be in the position of a nominative, because (ذا) is not intended with it. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the sentence as printed is elliptical.]»

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا خَيْراً: al-Kisāʾī said: and if (خير) [nominative] had been said, it would be permissible — meaning according to what has preceded. وَلَنِعْمَ دارُ الْمُتَّقِينَ: [دارُ is] nominative by (نعم). (الدار) is feminine, and He did not say (نعمت) because it is a verb resembling nouns; the view of the Basrans runs along these lines, and omitting the feminine marker is better according to them. Al-Kisāʾī said: the masculine is because the meaning is "and excellent is the place of the abode of the God-fearing", and [likewise] a dwelling (مثوى) and a refuge (مأوى).
He said: and the feminine is good, fine and widely used.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها: al-Farrāʾ said: if you wish, you put (جنات) in the nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), and if you wish, by the returning pronoun in (يدخلونها). The nominative according to the Basrans is from two directions: one is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the other with an implied mubtadaʾ, as you say: نعم الرجل زيد ("Excellent is the man — Zayd").

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (المتقين). طَيِّبِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. believers, avoiding sins.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: [هَلْ] يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: «أن» [is in the position of a nominative]; the angels with the punishment they were promised. [أَ]وْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ: with the punishment. And al-Kisāʾī related: حرص يحرص. «[Translator's note: the text of this entry is defective in the source (letters missing at the start of the quotations, and the grammatical comment on «أن» incomplete); the bracketed parts are the translator's restoration. The remark on حرص يحرص concerns verse 37, إِنْ تَحْرِصْ.]»

nahhas-irab:37-38.t: We have mentioned فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ. وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object]. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: if it had been said وعد عليه حقّ [in the nominative], it would be correct, i.e. "that is a promise binding upon Him, true".

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read إنّما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون with the accusative [فيكونَ]. Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is from two directions: one is by conjunction, i.e. "and that it be"; the other is that it is the answer to (كن). Abū Jaʿfar said: the [proper] way is that «فيكون» is nominative, and its implied structure according to Sībawayh is "and it is", while the accusative by conjunction is permissible. As for its being an answer, that is impossible, because it is a statement in which an answer is not permissible, just as you say: "I say to ʿAmr: go, and he sits", or "and he goes"; an answer has no meaning here — an answer would only be to say: "Go, and I will honour you."
And like the first is فَلا تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ [al-Baqara: 102], whereas the answer would only be "Do not disbelieve, lest you enter the Fire."

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا: that is, they abandoned their people and their homes in order to distance themselves from disbelief. وَالَّذِينَ is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ is in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا is in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute) from (الذين هاجروا), and [could be] in the position of an accusative as a badal from (هم).

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ ما نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ: that is, of the obligations, rulings and prescribed limits.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ is conjoined to the first. فِي تَقَلُّبِهِمْ: what they move about in, of journeys and other things.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ: because He granted them respite [and] called them to repentance.

nahhas-irab:48-49.t:
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّؤُا ظِلالُهُ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ: a singular in the place of a plural; وَالشَّمائِلِ is a plural in its regular sense. سُجَّداً is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. submissive and humbled to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has disposed for it. The root meaning of prostration (السجود) in the language is humbling oneself and submission. وَهُمْ داخِرُونَ: i.e. submissive, whether they like it or dislike it. And likewise prostration in وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دابَّةٍ, i.e. submissive to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pointing to His wisdom, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbās:
"The disbeliever prostrates to other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while his shadow prostrates to Allah, Blessed and Exalted", i.e. it submits to His disposing. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of "his shadow" here is his body from which the shadow comes, i.e. his body, flesh and bones are submissive to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, showing the trace of submission and humility upon them; on this basis it is prostrating to Him, holy be His name.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: وَالْأَنْعامَ is accusative by an implied verb, and the nominative is permissible outside the Qur'an.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ: Abū Isḥāq said: He mentioned (اثنين) as an emphasis (tawkīd) of (إلهين), just as He mentioned (واحدا) as an emphasis in His saying إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ. Others said: the implied structure is "and do not take two [as] gods".
فَإِيَّايَ is in the position of an accusative by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: وَلَهُ الدِّينُ واصِباً: [واصِباً is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: وَما بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: «ما» is in a conditional (jazāʾ) position, as if He said: "whatever blessing there is with you, it is from Allah". Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "and whatever blessing has come upon you is from Allah", i.e. whatever He has given you of bodily health or provision — all of that is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t:
وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِما لا يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيباً: that is, they assign to what they do not know to be a god a share of what We have provided them.
تَاللَّهِ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَفْتَرُونَ: that is, about your saying that they are gods.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ الْبَناتِ سُبْحانَهُ: because they said the angels are the daughters of Allah. The utterance is complete at His saying سُبْحانَهُ; then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلَهُمْ ما يَشْتَهُونَ, i.e. the thing which they desire, and «ما» is in the position of a nominative. Al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be in the position of an accusative, in the sense of "and they assign to themselves". Abū Isḥāq said: «ما» is in the position of a nominative and nothing else, because the Arabs do not say in the like of this جعل فلان له كذا ("So-and-so assigned to him such-and-such", meaning himself); they only say جعل لنفسه ("he assigned to himself"); and similar is ضربت نفسي ("I struck myself"), whereas one does not say ضربتني.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
وَإِذا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِالْأُنْثى ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا: [مُسْوَدًّا is] the khabar of «ظلّ». And according to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, ظلّ وجهه مسودّ is permissible, with a pronoun implied in «ظلّ» and the clause being the khabar. Sībawayh related:
«…until his parents are the ones who make him a Jew or make him a Christian» [with هما اللذان in the nominative]. Al-Farrāʾ said: [it is] like وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ تَرَى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ [al-Zumar: 60]. The original of (ظلّ) is (ظلل), then it was assimilated.
أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلى هُونٍ: al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is: he does not know, considering whether أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلى هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرابِ.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: وَلِلَّهِ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلى: that is, He is the One, the Self-Sufficient. الْحَكِيمُ: the All-Powerful, who neither begets nor was begotten. «[Translator's note: so in the source; الْحَكِيمُ is glossed with «القدير». The verse ends وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ.]»

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِمْ: that is, with the punishment of their wrongdoing. ما تَرَكَ عَلَيْها مِنْ دَابَّةٍ: because if He annihilated the fathers, offspring would be cut off.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t:
وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ: [ألسنة is] the plural of (لسان) according to the dialect of those who treat (اللسان) as masculine; whoever treats it as feminine says:
(ألسن). And whoever says (ألسن) and then names a man (لسان) does not decline it fully, but if he says (ألسنة) he declines it fully. (الكذب) is accusative by (تصف), and أَنَّ لَهُمُ is a badal (substitute) from (الكذب). Abū Ḥātim said: the people of Syria, or some of them, read وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ [i.e. الكُذُبُ in the nominative], as a naʿt (adjective) of (الألسنة). «[Translator's note: the variant (الكُذُبُ) is not vowelled in the source, which prints the ordinary reading; the following words «أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنى» are printed before «نعت للألسنة» as part of the verse.]» Quṭrub said: «أنّ لهم النار» is in the position of a nominative, i.e. "that has become binding". Others said: «أنّ» is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "that earned them «that theirs is the Fire»". We have mentioned the meaning of لا جَرَمَ. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on them both, read — and this reading is the reading of Abū Rajāʾ and Nāfiʿ — وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ with kasra on the rāʾ and without doubling «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket after the quotation.]»; and Abū Jaʿfar read وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ with kasra on the rāʾ and doubling. Abū Ḥātim said: it is related from Abū Jaʿfar وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ with fatḥa on the rāʾ and doubling. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read — and it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and the Kufans — وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ with fatḥa on the rāʾ and without doubling. «[Translator's note: the source prints all four readings identically as مُفْرَطُونَ; the distinctions are those stated in the words: مُفْرِطُونَ, مُفَرِّطُونَ, مُفَرَّطُونَ, مُفْرَطُونَ.]» The root of all this is from overstepping and going ahead. So (مفرطون) [mufriṭūn] means those who go to excess and overstep in evil; and from it one says: "So-and-so has gone to excess against So-and-so". «مفرّطون» [mufarriṭūn] means those who neglect and overstep what is obligatory; and from it is أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرّطت في جنب الله [al-Zumar: 56], and the doubling carries the sense of intensification and multiplicity. And «مفرطون» [mufraṭūn] means those sent ahead to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: تَاللَّهِ: the tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw, and one only says (تالله) when there is a sense of wonder in the utterance. لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلى أُمَمٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ: the object is omitted, i.e. messengers. فَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أَعْمالَهُمْ: that is, of disbelief and sins. فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and the ḍamma may be dropped for its heaviness, so one says فهو وليّهم [i.e. فَهْوَ], i.e. he is with them. And it was said: the meaning is that it will be said to them: "This one whom you obeyed — ask him to rescue you", by way of rebuke and reproach to them.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً: a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). Abū Isḥāq said: and the nominative is permissible, in the sense of "and it is, besides that, guidance and mercy".

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً: that is, an indication of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the excellence of His disposing.
نُسْقِيكُمْ with fatḥa on the nūn is the reading of ʿĀṣim, Shayba and Nāfiʿ; نُسْقِيكُمْ with ḍamma on the nūn is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and the Kufans except ʿĀṣim. «[Translator's note: so in the source, with both forms printed identically; in the familiar transmission the attributions are the reverse (Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim read نَسقيكم; the rest نُسقيكم).]» Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: سقيته means "I handed him [drink] and he drank", and أسقيته means "I gave him a supply of water". Abū ʿUbayda said: they are two dialectal forms. Abū Jaʿfar said: سقيته may mean "I exposed him to drinking", أسقيته "I prayed for rain for him", and أسقيته "I gave him a supply of water"; and أسقيته means سقيته according to Abū ʿUbayda; so [one reads] نسقيكم with ḍamma — except that it is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: نسقيكم with fatḥa is more fitting to the meaning here. مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ: it is masculine, and the grammarians have four views about this. Among the best of them is the view of Sībawayh, that the Arabs speak of (الأنعام) with a singular predicate; then he cited the verse, as though he held that (الأنعام) is treated as masculine and feminine. Al-Kisāʾī said — al-Farrāʾ related it from him — the meaning is "We give you to drink of what is in the bellies of what We mentioned". Al-Farrāʾ said: (الأنعام) and (النعم) are the same, both being plurals, so it reverts to the masculine of (النعم); and it is related from the Arabs: هذا نعم وارد ("these are cattle coming to water", with the masculine). Abū ʿUbayd related this view from al-Kisāʾī and recited: [rajaz] 263-
أكلّ عام نعم تحوونه ... يلقحه قوم وتنتجونه
(Every year, cattle you seize, which one people impregnates and you bring to birth?)
The fourth view Abū ʿUbayd related from Abū ʿUbayda; he said: the meaning is "We give you to drink of what is in the bellies of whichever of them has milk", because not all of them have milk. سائِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ: a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: وَمِنْ ثَمَراتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالْأَعْنابِ: that is, "and for you, in what We have provided you of the fruits of date-palms and grapes, there is a lesson".

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: وَأَوْحى رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ أَنِ اتَّخِذِي: [feminine] because it is feminine; and the Arabs say in its diminutive (نحيل) without the hāʾ, so that it would not resemble the singular (one bee). Al-Akhfash related that it is treated as masculine. بُيُوتاً, as you say فلس and فلوس; and whoever gives kasra to the bāʾ [بِيوتا] substitutes kasra for the ḍamma, and that is a far-fetched option.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ: that is, to decrepitude, because it weakens his strength and his mind. If someone says: "He is like that when he is a child, yet one does not say of a child: he is in the most abject age", the answer is that for the child intelligence and strength are hoped for, and it is not so with decrepitude. لِكَيْ لا يَعْلَمَ: [يَعْلَمَ is] accusative by (كي), and «لا» does not intervene [as a barrier] between the governing word and what it governs, because of its flexibility and because it may be redundant (zāʾida).

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَواءٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
أَفَبِالْباطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ: it was said: it means the idols and statues, because they do not benefit from worshipping them.
وَبِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ هُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ: ingratitude for a blessing in the language is of two kinds: one is to deny the blessing, and the other is to ascribe it to other than the one who bestowed it, or to make for Him a partner in it.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t:
وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِنَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ شَيْئاً: concerning the accusative of (شيء) there are two views. One is that the implied structure is "they are not able to provide them with anything", and this is the view of the Kufans. According to al-Akhfash and others of the Basrans, it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (رزق). Al-Akhfash said: and the meaning is:
"they do not possess for them any provision, little or much". Others said: it is not permissible for it to be accusative by (رزق), because it is a noun, not a maṣdar (verbal noun), just as it is not permissible to say عجبت من دهن زيد لحيته ("I wondered at Zayd's oil his beard") until you say من دهن [as a maṣdar, "Zayd's oiling his beard"]. «[Translator's note: the distinction is between دُهن (oil, a noun) and دَهن (oiling, a maṣdar), not marked in the source.]»
وَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ: according to the sense, because «ما» refers in meaning to a group.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t:
فَلا تَضْرِبُوا لِلَّهِ الْأَمْثالَ: there are two views about it. One: do not liken Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His creation, so that you say:
"He needs a partner and a counsellor", for this is only for one who does not know; and indicating this is إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ. The other view: do not liken the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to Him, so that you ascribe to them majesty like His.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا عَبْداً مَمْلُوكاً لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ: that is, because of slavery. وَمَنْ رَزَقْناهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً: that is, just as these two are not equal in your view, so they must not make the idols — which neither understand nor benefit — equal to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in worship. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: that is, for His guiding us to His oneness. بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: there are two views about it: one is that their action is the action of one who does not know, even though they know; and the other is that they do not know, though it is incumbent upon them to know.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُما أَبْكَمُ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ: and when he is mute and weak, he is a burden on his guardian; wherever he directs him, i.e. if he directs him to some worldly benefit, he brings no good. هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ: [مَنْ is] conjoined to the pronoun in (يستوي), and (هو) is an emphasis (tawkīd). Conjoining to the nominative pronoun became good when you emphasized it, because the emphasis supports it, so it is as though it were separate from the verb.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُمْ مِنْ بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ: whoever gives kasra to the hamza [إِمَّهاتكم] makes the kasra follow the kasra; and giving kasra to the mīm is far-fetched. (أمّهات) is the plural of (أمّهة); and it was said: the hāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), just as it was added in (أهرقت).

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ: that is, to their creation — how they were created with a constitution enabling them to fly and to remain steady in the air; and He made that a subjection from Him for them, figuratively, saying, exalted be His praise: مُسَخَّراتٍ فِي جَوِّ السَّماءِ; and مُسَخَّراتٍ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: because He, Mighty and Majestic, holds them steady by the air He created beneath them, so He made that a holding of them on His part, by extension of usage.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
وَالْخَيْلَ وَالْبِغالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ: that is, "and He made for you". Al-Farrāʾ said: it refers back to (خلق).
He said: and if you wish, it may mean "and He subjected". He said: and the nominative is permissible in two ways: one is that, since no verb is with it, you put it in the nominative; the other is that, since (والأنعام) in the nominative is permissible, you imagined it to be nominative and so put [these] in the nominative. وَزِينَةً: al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "and He made them an adornment". Al-Farrāʾ said: and it is permissible to put it in the accusative by the verb itself, its implied sense being "that you may ride them as an adornment". Abū Ḥātim said: Saʿīd related from Qatāda, from Abū ʿIyāḍ, that he read لتركبوها زينة without the wāw. Abū Isḥāq said: «زينة» is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. He created them for the sake of adornment.
Abū Isḥāq said: everything that grows on the earth is called (شجر). Isrāʾīl related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ — he said: "you pasture [your livestock]". Abū Isḥāq said: it is derived from (السّومة), i.e. the mark, because when they graze they leave traces on the ground, so that marks appear on it.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ: that is, He created for you that from which you make garments, and enabled you to make them. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read كذلك تتمّ نعمه عليكم, with (النعمة) in the nominative.
لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ: [and he read it] with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the lām [i.e. تَسْلَمُونَ].

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنْكِرُونَها: their denial of it is their ascribing it to other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and their associating others with Him in it.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً: (الأمة) is the generation and the group. He thereby indicated that in every generation there is one who obeys Him, Mighty and Majestic, and the witness can only be obedient. ثُمَّ لا يُؤْذَنُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: in offering excuses. The meaning of "they are not permitted to offer excuses" is that it is not said to them "offer excuses"; rather it is said to them: "If you offer excuses, it will not be accepted from you." And similar is وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ [al-Mursalāt: 36], i.e. they will not offer an excuse that would benefit them.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: وَإِذا رَأَى الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا شُرَكاءَهُمْ: that is, their idols which they used to worship, gathered with them so that they may be rebuked and reproached by them in the Fire. He called them "their partners" because they assigned to them a share of their wealth, their crops and their livestock. فَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلَ: they were made to speak and said to them: "You lied; we were not gods, nor do we deserve worship."

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ السَّلَمَ: they surrendered and submitted. وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ: it perished and vanished.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ زِدْناهُمْ عَذاباً فَوْقَ الْعَذابِ: that is, above the punishment they deserved for their disbelief. بِما كانُوا يُفْسِدُونَ: by their turning people away from Islam.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: تِبْياناً: that is, an explanation (بيانا), like (تلقاء). And one says (تبيانا) with fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. clarifying (تبيينا).

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ: that is, fairness. وَالْإِحْسانِ: that is, generosity beyond what is due. The real meaning of (الإحسان) in the language is every good act. وَإِيتاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبى: and that is maintaining the ties of kinship. وَيَنْهى عَنِ الْفَحْشاءِ: and that is every ugly act or word. وَالْمُنْكَرِ: everything that minds reject, of acts or words. وَالْبَغْيِ: the worst corruption. Al-Qāsim ibn Sallām related that one says: برأ جرحه على بغي ("his wound healed with baghy"), when it healed while some festering remained in it. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ; the original is (تتذكّرون), with the tāʾ assimilated into the dhāl.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: وَأَوْفُوا: according to the dialect of those who say (أوفى); and one also says وفى بعهد الله. إِذا عاهَدْتُمْ: there are two views about it: one is "with what He has charged you with and enabled you to do"; the other is "fulfil what you have sworn to", and this is more fitting and closer to the meaning, because after it comes وَلا تَنْقُضُوا الْأَيْمانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِها. Al-Kisāʾī said: many people of the Arabs say (تأكيد) and (قد أكّدت). Abū Isḥāq said: the original is the wāw, and the hamza is a substitute for it. وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا: their saying "Allah is guarantor and witness over this"; and it may be figurative, so that their swearing is like their saying this.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَها: that is, so that you undo what you have confirmed and strengthened. مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ: the Arabs call a firmly twisted strand (قوة). Abū Isḥāq said: أَنْكاثاً signifies the maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of (نقض) and (نكث) is the same. He said: and دَخَلًا is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). أَنْ is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is "because one community is more numerous than another" — from ربا الشيء يربو when it increases. Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "for one community to be" — [and that is] a dialectal usage. «[Translator's note: the source reads «لأن تكون لغة»; the text appears defective, possibly for «لأن تكون أمة» ("because a community should be"). Translated as written.]» Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: أَرْبى is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is like تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً [al-Muzzammil: 20]; they both make «هو» a support pronoun (ʿimād). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, and not permissible; it does not resemble تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً, because the hāʾ in «تجدوه» is definite while (أمة) is indefinite. According to both of them, ما كان أحد هو جالس is not permissible. Al-Khalīl said: (هو) is not redundant except with a definite noun, and according to him its being redundant with a definite noun is remarkable — so how could it be added with an indefinite? So the [correct] view is that «أربى» is in the position of a nominative because it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the khabar of (تكون).

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ: the answer to the prohibition; and the meaning is "so that it becomes deserving of punishment after having been deserving of reward".

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: ما عِنْدَكُمْ is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يَنْفَدُ is in the position of the khabar (predicate). وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ باقٍ: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. We have mentioned the like of (باق) [before].

nahhas-irab:98-99.t:
فَإِذا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ: its figurative sense (majāz) is [when you intend to recite]. «[Translator's note: the explanation of the majāz is missing in the source; the bracketed words are the translator's.]» إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ سُلْطانٌ: it comes with (السلطان) treated as masculine, while many of the Arabs treat it as feminine, saying: قضت به عليك السلطان ("the authority decreed it against you"). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that Satan has no authority over the believers, and He, Mighty and Majestic, made known in another place that he has no authority over anyone.
As for the meaning of إِنَّما سُلْطانُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ: it is that when he whispers to them, they accept from him.
